newsitem.title: POLAND: Administrative reform threatens Polish coalition.
newsitem.headline: Administrative reform threatens Polish coalition.

text.p: The Peasants Party threatened on Thursday to quit Poland's ruling coalition if its partner in government, the former communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), went ahead with a radical reform of the administrative system.
The party has made several such threats during the three years of the coalition's uneasy existence.
The coalition commands nearly two-thirds of the seats in parliament, but analysts said the withdrawal of the Peasants Party would almost certainly precipitate early elections.
The reform would introduce a new mid-level administrative unit, called Powiat, ran by locally-elected administrations.

"If we continue to see the idea of Powiat enforced, then we do not see any possibility of participating in the coalition and this will not be our fault," Senate Speaker Adam Struzik, a senior Peasants Party official, told a news conference.

Analysts say the Peasants Party is against the reform, which would also reduce the number of provinces from the current 49, because it could lose some of the strong influence it has in local government under the existing system.
